05/30/2023
Claim received by phone from the insured's representing attorney's office reporting a low-speed collision in a parking
lot. Claimant is represented, so all contact will route through counsel going forward.
07/16/2023
Reviewed the policy declarations and confirmed the driver involved is named on the policy and the coverage was in
force at the time of loss.
07/26/2023
Obtained the police report, which places the claimant in the vehicle at the scene and records the same general
sequence of events the claimant described.
08/02/2023
Spoke with the other driver, who confirmed the accident happened as described and had no disagreement about how
the vehicles came together.
08/10/2023
Collected three witness statements and several scene photos. All of them line up with the claimant's account of the
impact.
09/17/2023
Inspected the claimant's vehicle. The damage pattern is consistent with the impact described, and there is no sign of
earlier damage to the same areas.
09/20/2023
Ran a prior-claims search and found no earlier ijnury claims or treatment involving the same body area for this
claimant.
10/03/2023
Counsel sent the initial injury report describing neck strain. The reported symptoms fit the kind and force of this
collision well.
10/24/2023
Claimant's recorded statement was taken through counsel. Several small details were added compared with the first
account, but the core story did not change.
10/27/2023
Medical records show a treatment course running somewhat longer than is typical for a neck strain of this kind.
Requested the provider's notes to understand the timeline of visits.
11/25/2023
Reviewed the porvider notes and billing with the medical reviewer. The treatment is documented and linked to the
reported injury, and the length of care is noted for the file.
12/29/2023
Current status: liability and coverage are accepted, the vehicle damage is recorded, and the injury evaluation is
ongoing with counsel. Next step is to finalize the medcial review before setting an offer.
</page>

Rate each feature below that THIS page gives evidence about. Leave out a feature the page
says nothing about. The ratings are listed from least to most suspicious.
- injury_crash_fit: Does the claimed injury fit the type and force of the crash? Allowed: Strong, Reasonable, Unclear, Inconsistent.
- treatment_growth: Did the treatment grow beyond what this injury needs? Allowed: Normal, Elevated, Disproportionate, Extreme.
- pre_existing_condition: Did an earlier condition of the same body area add to the complaints? Allowed: None, Minor, Material, Predominant.
- occurrence_support: Do independent sources (witnesses, photos, cameras, the other driver) confirm that the accident happened as described? Allowed: Confirmed, Partially corroborated, Uncorroborated, Contradicted, Suspected staged.
- damage_crash_fit: Does the vehicle damage fit the described impact? Allowed: Strong, Reasonable, Unclear, Inconsistent.
- account_stability: Did the claimant's account of the accident stay the same over time? Allowed: Stable, Clarified, Materially changed.
- occupant_presence: Was the claimant really in the vehicle at the time of the crash? Allowed: Verified, Unclear, Added later, Not present.
- prior_damage_evidence: Is there evidence of vehicle damage from before this crash? Allowed: None, Possible, Documented, Material.
- known_loss_evidence: Is there evidence the damage existed or was known before the coverage started? Allowed: Weak, Moderate, Strong.
- driver_status: Is the driver of the insured vehicle on the policy? Allowed: Listed, Household, Unlisted, Excluded.

For each rated feature give:
- "rating": exactly one of the allowed ratings,
- "confidence": "High", "Medium" or "Low" (how clearly the page shows it),
- "quote": one or two sentences copied EXACTLY from the page that support the rating, with any
  spelling errors as they are,
- "reason": one short sentence.
